assumptions: External wrench sensing, IMU, and inertial model are calibrated for torque estimation.
The position-servo actuator map is identified and monitored over direction, speed, and temperature.
environments: model-based humanoid control on high-ratio position-controlled joints
robots: HRP-2 in the paper; other position-controlled robots require independent identification
simulators: Rigid-body dynamics models used for estimator and upper-level controller validation

confidence_rationale: The paper provides an identified actuator model and HRP-2 trajectory/force experiments, while pinned TSID code confirms the separate upper-level inverse-dynamics layer. Confidence is capped because the low-level map is platform- and condition-specific and is not fully represented by modern TSID code.

evidence.locator: Actuator identification in Figure 1 and Tables 1-3; force-control Figure 5
evidence.note: Shows the estimated torque-to-position-offset bridge and quantified HRP-2 tracking behavior.
Confirms that TSID supplies upper-level task-space inverse dynamics rather than the paper's full HRP-2 estimator and actuator mapping.

question: WBC/TSID 已经算出期望关节力矩，为什么位置控制机器人仍不能直接执行？
statement: 期望力矩只是上层动力学答案；高减速比位置控制关节还需要经传感与逆动力学估计、平台辨识和受限位置偏置，把期望力矩映射到可验证的执行接口。HRP-2 的辨识结果不能直接复制到其他机器人，也不能等同于真实关节力矩传感。
